'''MA-13'''<ref name="Droid Factory">{{DisneyToyCite|set=Star Wars: Droid Factory (toy line)|packtype=Multipack|pack=R6-D3 · MA-13 · R1 · N0-AH|altlink=https://wdwnt.com/2021/12/photos-new-the-mandalorian-droid-factory-set-now-available-at-disneys-hollywood-studios}}</ref> was a [[ferry droid]] that operated a [[keelboat]] along a [[Magma|lava]] [[Underground lava river|river]] on the [[planet]] [[Nevarro]]. The [[Color|orange]] and white ferry [[droid]] had the appearance of an [[R-series]] [[astromech droid]], though it had been [[Monster droid|modified]] to have [[Limb|legs]] and two sets of arms, which he used to row the [[boat]] down the river. When [[Din Djarin]], [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]], [[Greef Karga]], and [[IG-11]] were attempting to [[Clash on Nevarro|escape]] [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]'s [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|forces]] with [[Din Grogu|Grogu]], they boarded the droid's keelboat, and the droid began to take them downriver. However, Djarin noticed a number of [[stormtrooper]]s waiting for them at the end of the tunnel, and Dune urged the droid to stop the boat. When the droid continued to row, Dune shot the droid's head off, but his destruction did not stop the boat from moving.<ref name="Chapter 8" />

{{Droid-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
MA-13 first appeared unnamed in "[[Chapter 8: Redemption]]," the eighth episode of [[The Mandalorian Season One|season one]] of the [[2019]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', directed by [[Taika Waititi]] and released on [[Disney+]]<ref name="Chapter 8" /> on [[December 27]], 2019.<ref name="DTCI">{{WebCite|url=https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/documents/the_mandalorian_project_one-sheet_10_ec1e005f.pdf|text=The Mandalorian Media Kit|date=2019-09-24|format=[[Wikipedia:PDF|PDF]]|work=[[Wikipedia:Walt Disney Direct-to-Consumer & International|Walt Disney Direct-to-Consumer & International]]|pages=[https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/documents/the_mandalorian_project_one-sheet_10_ec1e005f.pdf#page=1]|archivedate=20210623202717}}</ref> Digital concept art for the droid was done by [[Ryan Church]], based on an unused design done by [[Matt Allsopp]] in October [[2013]] as a farm droid for the [[Erso homestead]]  for the film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',<ref name="Chapter 8 Guide">{{SW|url=series/the-mandalorian/chapter-8-guide|text="Redemption" Episode Guide | The Mandalorian}} {{C|Trivia Gallery Slide 2}}</ref> which was ultimately replaced with the [[SE-2 worker droid]].<ref name="UVG">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''</ref> Church described MA-13 as a "[[Wikipedia:Styx|Stygian]] [[R2-series astromech droid|R2 unit]],"<ref name="Church">{{Instagram|username=ryanchurchart|url=p/CL7ANGPjfov|name=[[Ryan Church]]|quote=#TheMandalorian - a Stygian R2 unit- there's something so perfectly, mythically Star Wars about crazy stuff like this...based on a @cuppasketch design... @taikawaititi awesome season 1 finale, for Design Supervisor @doug_chiang and Dave Filoni|archiveurl=https://archive.is/EOlMb}}</ref> referencing one of the rivers of the [[Wikipedia:Greek underworld|underworld]] in ancient [[Wikipedia:Greek mythology|Greek mythology]].

The droid was subsequently identified in the form of an action figure released by [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] in [[2021]] as part of a set with three other droids from ''The Mandalorian'' as part of the [[Star Wars: Droid Factory (toy line)|''Star Wars: Droid Factory'']] toy line.<ref name="Droid Factory" /> Although the episode features MA-13's [[death]], the [[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 1|graphic novel]] of season one depicts him surviving the events.<ref name="MandoGN">[[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 1|''The Mandalorian'' – The Graphic Novel of Season 1]]</ref>
